pipeline.name: Healthcare_Data_AI_pipeline
pipeline.description: Integrated CKM drug-side-effect pipeline (Stage 1 drug screen -> Stage 2 side-effect model), Korea (NHIS Sample Cohort) and Japan (JMDC claims).
pipeline.generated_by: written by hand alongside core/R and countries/*, not auto-derived -- keep in sync manually if a table's shape changes

database.note: Both countries' Stage 1 write to this ONE database, using different table-name conventions to avoid colliding -- see 'tables' below.

cohort_processed.description: Stage 1 output: one row per CKM stage 2/3 cohort member, with covariates, competing-risks outcome flags/dates, and follow-up end.

columns.index_date: date, first health-checkup date in the study window
columns.age: integer, age at index (band-midpoint approximation, see CLAUDE.md)
columns.death_date: date, nullable -- month-end approximation of NHID_JK.DTH_YM

columns.index_date: date, first annual health-checkup date in the study window
columns.age: integer, exact age at index (from birth month/year)
columns.note: NO separate death_date column (unlike Korea) -- Stage 2 approximates death_date := followup_end when died_in_data is TRUE. See CLAUDE.md 'Known asymmetries'.

drug_exposure.description: Stage 1 output: one row per (patient, ATC code) with PDC (Proportion of Days Covered) during the 1-year baseline lookback; exposed = PDC > 0.8.

cox_results.description: Stage 1 output: single-drug-at-a-time Cox screen, one row per (ATC code, outcome). SAME column names for both countries (core/R/cox_screen.R emits this shape uniformly) -- this is what core/R/candidate_drugs.R reads automatically as Stage 2's candidate-drug hand-off.

columns.hr: double, hazard ratio for exposed vs. unexposed
columns.n_event: integer, events in the fitted model
columns.candidate: boolean, TRUE when hr > 1.00 AND p_value < 0.05

demo_data.description: Synthetic (NOT real patient data) stand-in for Stage 1's output, used by `Rscript countries/<country>/run_pipeline.R --demo`. See data/generate_synthetic_data.R for the generation method -- 3 of 15 simulated ATC codes carry a real embedded excess hazard and are the only ones marked candidate == TRUE in the synthetic cox_results, so a demo run exercises genuine (if synthetic) signal, not pure noise.
